category_title: Students with learning disabilities who manage fast-paced lectures by focusing on discrete information categories
student_description: Sandra is a 7th-grade student who becomes easily overwhelmed by the cognitive load of fast-paced science lectures. When she tries to transcribe everything verbatim, she falls behind and misses large chunks of information. She uniquely requires concrete, categorized note-taking structures, pre-lecture priming, and explicit cues to help her filter out extraneous details and focus on discrete tasks.

criteria.rationale: Breaking note-taking into discrete, shifting tasks helps Sandra manage cognitive load over time without feeling overwhelmed by trying to capture everything at once.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan includes teaching Sandra to isolate specific note-taking tasks (e.g., focusing only on definitions for one lecture) and shift her focus based on changing demands.

criteria.rationale: Sandra needs sustained, guided practice to learn how to apply note-taking strategies effectively under the temporal pressure of normal lecture speeds.
criteria.check: The tutor's long-term plan incorporates explicit modeling and guided practice specifically designed to gradually acclimate Sandra to taking notes at a standard lecture pace.
